summary.headline: Bajaj Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores and PAT 26.9% to INR14.1 crores, with formulations up 82%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores in Q2 FY27 and 6.2% QoQ, with H1 revenue up 15.1% to INR341.5 crores. EBITDA rose 12.2% YoY to INR32.1 crores at an 18.2% margin, while gross margin fell to 48.3% amid West Asia disruption. Formulations (INR41.7 crores, up 82% YoY) and export API (INR62.6 crores, up 28.5%) offset a weaker domestic API line (INR71.6 crores, down from INR76.3 crores). Management reiterated FY29 targets of INR900-1,000 crores revenue and 18-21% EBITDA margin, and flagged higher inventory held as a precaution against Gulf disruption.

segments.name: Domestic API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR71.6 crores vs INR92 crores in Q1 and INR76.3 crores a year ago; H1 up 10.1% YoY to INR163.9 crores. Management expects little pricing improvement over time.

segments.name: Export API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR62.6 crores, up 28.5% YoY; Magnesium L-Threonate supplied to a US patent holder contributes about 11-12% of total turnover.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR41.7 crores, up about 82% YoY, driven by the Cenobamate API tablet launch in September through eight marketing partners; formulations are about 24% of revenue in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY29 target: revenue of INR900-1,000 crores with EBITDA margin of 18-21%.
Management said it is on track for the earlier guidance of 10-15% revenue and profit growth with 18-20% margin; Q2 growth was almost 20%.
Operating cash flow expected to be more than INR30 crores for FY27.
Total FY27 capex expected at INR65-80 crores; about INR50-60 crores per year thereafter to reach INR1,000 crores revenue.
Management expects gross margin and EBITDA margin to be maintained in coming quarters, supported by product mix.

Genrx (acquired, NCLT approved): INR200-250 crores revenue potential in two to three years. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after commissioning in Q2 FY28. Peptide facility: first-year revenue INR70-100 crores in FY28-29.
capex_capacity: Peptide manufacturing plant (250 kg per annum, solid-phase synthesis and fermentation) scheduled for completion by 31 March 2027.
Oncology API plant to commence in Q2 FY28.
Dedicated formulation plant at Nashik (solid oral dosage, nasal, oral oncology, nutraceutical, ointment) expected operational in Q1 FY28.
New R&D centre started in August with over 80 staff, planned capacity of 120 chemists; R&D spend raised to about 2.5-3% of revenue.
Genrx acquisition to handle non-Baroda formulation volumes; new molecules to be made at Baroda, which is an approved facility.
demand_pricing: Cenobamate API tablets approved by DCGI (first in India, six strengths), launched commercially in September 2026; repeat orders received from partners, but secondary sales not yet known.

Regulatory filings: 110 DMFs filed, with approvals taking two to three years; 8 CEPs approved and 4 under review in Europe; 17 products registered with KDMF in South Korea; 3 products registered in Egypt with 10 more planned; 17 products identified for Brazil CBPF submission.
API pricing described as under pressure with little prospect of improvement; management said prices are more or less stabilised but volatile given Gulf disputes, freight and interest rates.
Management expects 60-70% of the portfolio to be backward integrated in two to three years.
Mix target over three to four years: formulations 45-50% and API 50-55% (vs about 20-24% formulations today).

qa_highlights.question: Will Manjusar formulation production shift to Genrx, and what is the role of the Nashik facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Nashik is a strategic capacity addition for the next two to three years; new molecules will be made at the approved Baroda facility, and Genrx will handle other formulations for different markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital inventory rise and will it normalise by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the higher inventory is a deliberate policy decision to avoid stoppages from the Gulf dispute; management did not give a normalisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue potentials from Genrx and the oncology API plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Genrx: INR200-250 crores in two to three years after start-up. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after it is in operation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and is guidance on track?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR65-80 crores; CFO said the company is on track for the earlier 10-15% growth and 18-20% margin guidance, with Q2 growth near 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given weak H1 conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow expected above INR30 crores for FY27; Q2 operating cash flow about INR15 crores; receivable days improved from 145 to 135.

qa_highlights.question: How is EBITDA margin holding up despite a roughly 225-250 bp YoY gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed stable EBITDA margin to product mix: export and formulation (Cenobamate launch) offset the domestic API dip, and said margins are expected to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio can be backward integrated, and what are the margin effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70% of products could be backward integrated in two to three years, with revenue from these products rising about 10-15% and margins improving; no specific margin figure was given.

risks_watch: Gross margin fell YoY (about 225-250 bp per analyst) amid West Asia/Gulf disruption, freight and interest-rate pressure; management expects improvement but gave no figure.
Working capital and inventory build: operating cash flow in H1 weak relative to EBITDA; FY27 cash flow target of more than INR30 crores depends on inventory normalisation.
Domestic API revenue fell QoQ and YoY in Q2; API prices described as under pressure.
Commercial timelines: DMF/CEP approvals take 1-3 years; peptide and oncology plants depend on approvals with customers (6-10 months post-commissioning).
Cenobamate secondary sales not disclosed; management could not quantify FY27/FY28 revenue from it.
Execution risk from several new plants (peptide by March 2027, Nashik Q1 FY28, oncology Q2 FY28) and rapid senior hiring; management cited facilities as the main bottleneck over three years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and formulations, with specific targets for FY29 and plant timelines. More cautious and less specific on API pricing, working capital and cash conversion, which management tied to Gulf disruption.
key_quotes: Coming to the quarter, Q2 27 was a strong quarter.
Our formulation business rebounded strongly, growing 82% year -on-year, as we had expected at the end of Q1.
As you know, always API is always on pressure. Price pressure is there, even the demand pressure is there.
We are pretty confident of maintaining this gross margin and EBITDA margins.
